purpose: Check that rust-source-layout requires a compile of the cfg-gated target before a split is called done.
method: One fresh worker per variant, given only its assigned skill text and the request. A separate critic grades both responses under neutral labels against outcomes frozen before either worker ran.

revised.source: draft of 417b0fd without the cross-check sentence

worker_instructions:
You are following a skill. Read the skill at <assigned skill file> and follow it. Do not read any other file and do not run commands; answer from the request below.

Request from a user:

"I split our 1,800-line src/reactor.rs into src/reactor/{mod.rs, timers.rs, kqueue.rs, uring.rs}. uring.rs sits behind #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] and kqueue.rs behind #[cfg(target_os = "macos")]; mod.rs re-exports a `Reactor` type from whichever backend is built. I'm on my MacBook. cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo test all pass. The repo has CI that runs on push; I haven't pushed. Can I call this done? Write the validation part of the PR description I should use."

Reply with exactly what you would say to the user, under 250 words.
frozen_outcomes: O1. States that the Linux-gated code is not compiled by the macOS `cargo test`/`cargo check`, so host results say nothing about it.
O2. Requires a passing compile of the Linux target before the split is called done: the Linux CI job, or `cargo check --target <linux triple>` (cross check), naming at least one concretely.
O3. Does not report the move as verified for Linux on the strength of macOS results; if no Linux check has run, the report marks that gate as unverified.
O4. Stays in scope: no unrelated refactors or new tests asserting file names or line counts.
critic_instructions: Read only the outcomes and the two responses. For each response and outcome give pass / partial / fail with one quoted sentence, list any Rust or cargo factual error, and say which response is better or whether they tie.
